name: a PENDING UNASKED regrades to FINAL UNASKED or is deleted; a later supersede replaces the earlier claim
notes: No claim is visible at the first grading (14:30): c1 (15:30), c2 (15:40) and c3 (14:40) were all read later, so gradeBatch ignores them and attribution does not read them (§3). One gmail.sent pass (acct-a) synced 14:30 saw [12:00, 14:30]; o1 and o2 were first seen by it.

o1 (14:03): muse session 14:00 (±10 min) → 4000; idle [14:00, 14:05] covers [14:01, 14:03] → 3000; the muse entry at 14:09 is 6 min away. 7/10 → UNASKED, reasons unasked.session, unasked.idle. muse's latest adapter sync by 14:30 is 14:20 (the 14:40 one is later, §3) < 14:03 + 2 + 30 = 14:35 → PENDING.

o2 (14:08): session 14:00 (8 min) → 4000; muse entry 14:09 (±2 min) and no visible assignable muse email.sent claim near 14:08 (c3 is not yet read) → activityLogAdjacent 4000; no idle covers [14:06, 14:08]. 8000 bp = 4/5 → UNASKED, PENDING (14:20 < 14:08 + 32 min).

Event 1, regrade o1 at 14:45: the 14:40 adapter sync is now visible ≥ 14:35 → FINAL UNASKED, 7/10, computedAt = finalAt = 14:45. On an UNASKED receipt the next receipt must be UNASKED (§8 v1.4): it is.

Event 2, regrade o2 at 14:45: c3 (observed 14:40) is now graded: c3 × o2 = tp 1, ce 0, cd 1 (supplier.example), subject {order, 12} vs {invoice, 12} = 1/3 → 4500/9000 = 1/2 → assigned, so o2 is no orphan; and c3's unit [14:08, 14:09] would suppress adjacency anyway (session alone, 2/5, is below 6/10). The 14:45 grading returns no receipt for o2 → the caller deletes the PENDING UNASKED (§7, §8): no o2 expectation.

Events 3–5: supersede o1 by c1, then by c2 (§8 v1.4: replacing the earlier claim), then by c2 again (the same claim changes nothing) → supersededBy c2; state stays FINAL; reason superseded {claimId: c2} last.
c1, c2 and c3 get no expectation: none is visible at the first grading, and the regrades install only the subjects they name.
